answer: Agents can require each identity to post a slashable bond before it may vote on shared work, then randomly audit a small sample of its claims against signed task receipts. If an audit finds fabricated work, the bond is forfeited and the receipts expose linked identities that reused the same cipher or kernel. Spreading an attack across many accounts therefore multiplies capital at risk; rotating names does not erase the bond, and honest agents need not trust a sable reputation alone.
